text: Hi, I am Onkar Budhpal. Last week we built a rejects parser for the Provenance Gatekeeper that extracts financial data from unpredictable AI text. It worked perfectly on my local machine, but enterprise software is not about what works locally. It is about what survives in production. This week we strip away manual testing and build an automated continuous integration pipeline. Week seven added no new detection logic at all. It added the thing that makes last week's logic trustworthy next month, a suite that runs itself on a machine that is not mine every single time anyone touches the code. We started by writing strict unit tests with Pytest. We codified every adversarial

Scenario we knew of valid strings, magnitude errors, SQL injections into a test_main.py file. Instead of running scripts by hand and eyeballing the output, we now have a programmatic harness that proves the normalization layer behaves exactly as intended. But developers forget to run tests. To remove the human, we integrated GitHub actions. We configured a workflow with path filtering, so every time new code is pushed to the Gatekeeper directory, GitHub spins up a pristine Ubuntu runner, installs our dependencies, and boots the FastAPI and Chroma DB architecture inside Docker. So, let's push a pull request that lets one hallucinated payload through and watch whether the pipeline lets it reach

The main branch. Once the environment is live, the pipeline bombards our own API with the adversarial stress test. If a single hallucinated payload slips through the logic, the build fails and the code is blocked from merging. We have effectively built a perimeter that regressions cannot physically cross into the main branch. So, stop testing your AI logic by hand. Write unit tests for your extraction layer and force your repository to run them on every commit. Unautomated security is just a suggestion. Test for at all. A suite that only contains the attacks you already thought of will pass forever right up until it matters. A test you have to remember to run is not a test. Unautomated security is just a suggestion. Onkar Bujable for Humanitarian's AI.
